title: New Deoxygenation Threshold for N2 and N2O Production in Coastal Waters and Sediments
content:
Abstract

Bioavailable nitrogen governs ocean productivity and carbon fixation by regulating phytoplankton growth and community composition. Nitrogen input primarily results from N2 ${\mathrm{N}}_{2}$ fixation, while denitrification and anammox remove bioavailable nitrogen in oxygen-depleted conditions. Traditionally considered limited to highly suboxic (i.e., <5 μM) waters, recent studies suggest that fixed-nitrogen removal processes may extend beyond, elevating global nitrogen loss estimates. This study directly quantifies fixed-nitrogen loss across oxygen gradients (from 140 to 32 μM) along the Estuary and Gulf of St. Lawrence using N cycle tracers (N2/Ar ${\mathrm{N}}_{2}/\text{Ar}$, N∗ ${\mathrm{N}}^{\ast }$, and N2O ${\mathrm{N}}_{2}\mathrm{O}$). Notably, we observe significant N2 ${\mathrm{N}}_{2}$ production when ambient O2 ${\mathrm{O}}_{2}$ concentrations fall below a threshold value of 58.9 ± 1.1 μM, including potential water column fixed-nitrogen removal processes above suboxia. We hypothesis that ambient deoxygenation eases the formation of suboxic microareas in suspended organic matter. Benthic N2 ${\mathrm{N}}_{2}$ production remains unaffected under intensifying water column deoxygenation from 50 down to 32 μM, but the contribution of NO3− $\mathrm{N}{\mathrm{O}}_{3}^{-}$ produced through nitrification in the sediment to denitrification diminishes as deoxygenation intensifies. Combined, water column and benthic fixed-nitrogen removal processes drive N∗ ${\mathrm{N}}^{\ast }$ anomalies and strong NO3− $\mathrm{N}{\mathrm{O}}_{3}^{-}$ deficiency in bottom waters. Additionally, the observed O2 ${\mathrm{O}}_{2}$ threshold also triggers N2O ${\mathrm{N}}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ production. Overall, our study highlights the profound impact of coastal ocean deoxygenation on nitrogen cycling, suggesting unexpected shifts even at ambient oxygen concentrations traditionally considered well above suboxic conditions.
